title: The fender bass takeover and Wilbur Bascomb
summary: Hinton says the fender bass replaced him; they mention Bob Bushnell and the young Bascomb.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And the whole thing changed -- I certainly was replaced by the fender base, which came in, and I'm not a fender base player, and there were some great players then, though. What was that one that just died? Bob Bushnell, a very excellent fender base player and who were some of the others -- what's that guy's name who went to California?
Oh, yeah, I forgot his name now --
he is in California now. I can't remember. And then this young kid, Dud Bascomb? (Wilbur Bascomb -- ed.)
Dud Bascomb, Doug Baskin, yeah. His father's name was Doug Baskin also. What band was he in?
It was Erskine Hawkins' band. He's the guy that played that trumpet solo on "Tuxedo Junction" that everybody has to copy.
Right. And his son is one of the most excellent fender base players, and also acoustical base players, and a fine young man. Excellent young man.
